summary.text: A beneficiary can claim funeral expenses from the deceased’s un-nominated CPF monies. Claims of up to $6,000 are generally allowed.

details.heading: Proof of relationship
details.body: If you are the deceased’s spouse, provide the marriage certificate. If you are their child, provide your birth certificate and your parents’ marriage certificate. If you are their parent, provide the deceased’s birth certificate and your marriage certificate. If you are their sibling, provide the deceased’s and your birth certificates, and your parents’ marriage and death certificates.

details.heading: How payment is made
details.body: Payment is made to the claimant by PayNow registered with their NRIC, or by direct credit to a bank account. For payment by GIRO to a non-DBS or non-POSB bank account, provide a copy of the beneficiary’s bank passbook or statement showing the account and holder’s name. No documents are needed for payment by PayNow.

steps.name: Apply for reimbursement
steps.text: In the online application form, indicate how much you want to claim. Only a beneficiary can claim.

items: Indicate the amount of funeral expenses you want to claim in the online application form.
Only a beneficiary can claim reimbursement from the deceased’s un-nominated CPF monies.
Claims of up to $6,000 are generally allowed.

steps.name: Prepare supporting documents
steps.text: Prepare the documents that apply to you, including funeral receipts and the funeral expenses declaration form.

items: Provide relevant receipts for funeral expenses and the declaration form for funeral expenses.
Provide identification documents if you are not Singaporean.
Provide a death certificate if the deceased died outside Singapore.
Provide proof of your relationship to the deceased.

about.text: The relationship documents differ depending on whether you are the deceased’s spouse, child, parent or sibling.
